items.title: How, and why, to stress test your business case
items.summary: The opinions expressed by Trellis expert contributors are their own, not those of Trellis .2027 budget season is here, and it’s a tight one.

items.title: Updated: Sustainability tools to use in 2026
items.summary: Welcome to the Trellis roundup of new products and services for sustainability professionals, as chosen by our editorial team.

items.title: Two weeks to register: How to turn climate risk insights into adaptation action
items.summary: This webinar, held in partnership with SmartResilience on 19 November, will explore why and how leading organisations are moving from simply measuring risk to actively adapting in order to protect their operations, assets and supply chains.

items.title: UK to introduce mandatory human rights due diligence law for large businesses
items.summary: The UK Government will introduce mandatory human rights due diligence requirements for large businesses, requiring them to identify, assess and address risks of human rights abuses and labour exploitation in their operations and supply chains.

items.title: Apply now: Entries open for the edie Awards 2027
items.summary: The UK’s largest corporate sustainability awards scheme is celebrating its 20th year with a restructured programme, built around three pillars and new categories including AI, water and adaptation.

items.title: How AI can accelerate climate investment
items.summary: As sustainability teams face growing financial pressures and increasingly complex environmental markets, AI has emerged as a tool for identifying new investment opportunities, improving decision-making and securing internal buy-in.

items.title: Webinar next week: How to prepare for the UK Sustainability Reporting Standards
items.summary: This webinar, hosted in partnership with Simply Sustainable on 10 November, will explore how businesses can prepare for the UK Sustainability Reporting Standards (UK SRS), understand their current level of readiness and turn gaps into a practical implementation plan.

items.title: UNEP: Adaptation finance pledge falls 70% short for developing nations
items.summary: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) has warned that COP30’s goal of tripling adaptation finance by 2035 will not be enough to close the adaptation finance gap, leaving developing nations with, at most, 29% of what they need.

items.title: MPs warn Britain is “dangerously” dependent on China’s critical minerals
items.summary: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee has called on the Government to de-risk the country's critical dependencies in order to safeguard national and economic security.

items.title: Interactive: Tracking negotiating texts at the COP31 climate summit
items.summary: The centrepiece of every UN climate summit is for countries to negotiate the wording of a large number of legal agreements – and COP31 in the Turkish city of Antalya is no different.
